k-means uses Euclidean distance — features with large magnitudes dominate. Apply StandardScaler before KMeans: scaler = StandardScaler(); X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X). Without scaling, cluster recovery degrades significantly.

The dataset has 20 features but only 4 latent clusters. PCA before KMeans improves ARI: pca = PCA(n_components=10, random_state=42); X_reduced = pca.fit_transform(X_scaled). Ten components capture ~94% of variance and remove noise dimensions that confuse Euclidean distance.

Use KMeans(n_clusters=4, random_state=42, n_init=10). The ground truth has exactly 4 clusters (see make_blobs centers=4 in the brief). Call km.fit_predict(X_reduced) and return the labels array directly — adjusted_rand_score is permutation-invariant so label numbering does not matter.
